predecessors.name: Kingdom of Poland
predecessors.text: the western Greater Polish lands given to Mieszko III by Bolesław III's testament

successors.name: Kingdom of Poland
successors.text: the part of Greater Poland that Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland shape of 1305 covers (97 of the 111 cells)

successors.name: Duchy of Głogów
successors.text: 11 cells in the south-west that Cliopatria gives to Głogów in 1305

ledger.x: 1138: Bolesław III's testament gives Mieszko III the new Duchy of Greater Poland.
1173: Mieszko III becomes High Duke at Kraków.
1177: Casimir II of Sandomierz takes Kraków and the Seniorate from Mieszko III.
1181: Mieszko III conquers Gniezno and Kalisz.
1186: Mieszko III annexes Kuyavia when Leszek of Masovia dies.
1191: Mieszko III briefly retakes Kraków.
1191: Casimir II is High Duke again.
1195: the war for Kraków.
1198: Mieszko III wins Kraków by agreement.
1198: Mieszko III returns to Kraków as High Duke.
1199: Leszek the White is restored at Kraków.
1199: Kuyavia leaves Greater Poland.
1202: Władysław III Spindleshanks becomes Duke of Kraków and High Duke.
1206: Spindleshanks loses Kraków to Leszek the White.
1207: Kalisz is split off for Władysław Odonic.
1217: Kalisz returns to Spindleshanks' Greater Poland.
1228: Spindleshanks is elected High Duke at Wiślica.
1229: Spindleshanks loses the Seniorate to Konrad I of Masovia and Greater Poland to Odonic.
1234: Henry I the Bearded of Silesia invades Greater Poland.
22 September 1234: the settlement ends the war.
22 September 1234: Odonic gives up the south.
5 June 1239: Odonic dies and Henry II the Pious takes the rest of Greater Poland.
1241: Przemysł I and Bolesław the Pious begin to win back what their father lost.
1243: the brothers hold most of Poznań and Gniezno again.
1244: Kalisz is regained.
1247: Santok is regained from the Silesian line of Henry II the Pious.
1249: Wieluń is won.
1249: the reconquest is complete.
1265: Brandenburg takes Santok.
1270: Brandenburg takes Drezdenko.
1279: Przemysł II reunites Greater Poland.
ledger.cp: Duchy of Kalisz and Gniezno (Bolesław the Pious)

ledger.x: 1290: Przemysł II inherits Kraków.
1290: Przemysł II gives Kraków up to Wenceslaus II.
December 1294: Przemysł II inherits Gdańsk Pomerania.
26 June 1295: Przemysł II is crowned King of Poland at Gniezno.
1296: Brandenburg annexes Deutsch Krone.
8 February 1296: Przemysł II is murdered at Rogoźno and the Greater Polish Piast line ends.
1296: Gdańsk Pomerania passes out of Greater Poland's hands.
1297: Brandenburg annexes the Międzyrzecz castellany.
1300: the Piasts yield Greater Poland to Wenceslaus II of Bohemia.
1304: last year of the Cliopatria shape; the land passes to the Kingdom of Poland, Głogów and Brandenburg.

wars.name: Rebellion against Mieszko III and Casimir II's seizure of Kraków
wars.outcome: Casimir II took Kraków in 1177 (and Gniezno and Kalisz until Mieszko III won them back in 1181) while Mieszko's son Odon held Poznań and fought his father for almost two years.

wars.name: War for the Seniorate (Mozgawa)
wars.outcome: Mieszko III against the heirs of Casimir II (Leszek the White, his successor as High Duke, and the regency of Masovia): the battle of Mozgawa on 13 September 1195; in 1198 Mieszko returned to Kraków and ceded Kuyavia; deposed again in 1199.

wars.name: Spindleshanks-Odonic war
wars.outcome: Odonic took Ujście in October 1223 and Nakło in 1225, defeated his uncle in 1227 and, with Konrad I of Masovia, took all Greater Poland in 1229; Spindleshanks fled to Opole.

wars.name: Henry the Bearded's Greater Polish war
wars.outcome: Henry I the Bearded intervened in the summer of 1234; the terms published on 22 September 1234 made Odonic relinquish everything south and west of the Warta, Kalisz included.

wars.name: Henry II the Pious's war on Władysław Odonic
wars.outcome: Henry II the Pious (High Duke after Henry I's death on 19 March 1238) defeated Odonic in 1239; Odonic died on 5 June 1239 and Henry II took the rest of Greater Poland, leaving Odonic's sons Ujście and Nakło.

wars.name: Reconquest of Greater Poland by Przemysł I and Bolesław the Pious
wars.outcome: From 1241 the brothers regained most of Poznań and Gniezno by 1243, Kalisz in 1244, Santok in 1247 and Wieluń in 1249.

wars.name: Brandenburg's conquest of Santok and Drezdenko
wars.outcome: Brandenburg occupied Santok in early 1265 and captured Drezdenko in 1270; Cliopatria shows the loss from 1272.

wars.name: Przemysł II's Kraków succession
wars.outcome: Henry Probus willed Kraków to Przemysł II in 1290; he left in September-October 1290 and a synod gave Lesser Poland to Wenceslaus II for compensation.

wars.name: Greater Polish succession (1296-1300)
wars.outcome: After Przemysł II's murder the Greater Polish Piast line ended; Władysław I the Elbow-high took over (1296-1300) and in 1300 both Piasts renounced their claims in favour of Wenceslaus II of Bohemia.

wars.name: Brandenburg's annexation of Deutsch Krone and Międzyrzecz
wars.outcome: Brandenburg annexed Deutsch Krone in 1296 and the Międzyrzecz castellany in 1297 from Greater Poland.

certainty.note: A duchy of castellany districts: no page opened gives a surveyed or treaty boundary of the duchy as a whole.
